public_rationale: Supported on the plain reading that architectural depth does not guarantee deep understanding. The technical review describes processing layers and learned abstractions, while the original Go study shows that strong performance can coexist with unexpected failures. The textbook also describes learning hierarchies of concepts, so 'just' needs qualification. These sources support the distinction between architectural depth and guaranteed understanding; they do not support a claim that deep learning cannot learn concepts.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'entails' as 'guarantees', rather than as a denial of any conceptual learning.
The Go findings illustrate a limitation; they are not a direct test of conceptual depth.
Layer count is a simplified description of depth, whose technical definitions also involve composition and computational graphs.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that architectural depth does not itself guarantee deep understanding. 'Does not entail' does not mean that deep learning cannot learn concepts.
I interpret 'conceptual depth' as substantive understanding that extends beyond success on familiar examples. The speaker supplies no measurable threshold.

The claim concerns the established technical meaning and its implications as of the post. The target period has no specified beginning and ends on 2023-02-18; a quarterly reporting period would not fit this definitional claim.
The reference to a number of layers is treated as an ordinary description of architectural depth, not an exhaustive definition of every deep-learning architecture.
criteria.support_condition: Authoritative technical sources define depth through layers or composed computations, without making conceptual understanding a necessary consequence. Documented failures can support the distinction between task performance and reliable understanding.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Authoritative technical sources make substantive conceptual understanding a defining or guaranteed consequence of deep learning. Merely showing that some models learn useful concepts would not contradict the claim about entailment.

evidence.explanation: The technical description links deep learning to processing layers and learned abstractions. Reading this as an architectural description rather than a guarantee of understanding is the evaluator's inference.

The textbook explicitly connects deep learning with learning concepts. This qualifies 'just': it challenges a reading that denies conceptual learning altogether, but does not establish guaranteed conceptual understanding.

The original Go study supports the narrower point that strong performance can coexist with unexpected vulnerabilities. It does not measure conceptual depth or prove that the system lacks all conceptual representations.
